broadcast and send_removal_notice defer while the state lock is held and are flushed by poll outside the lock. Residual: overflow drops are silent, and deliver_incident still sends directly but is not reachable under the lock today.

evidence: pick_up_local_facts now takes the state lock first and holds it across the stamp check, load_facts (admission snapshot), read_lines (file scan), every quarantine_local_fact, receipt, apply and refold, and the final stamp update.

membership::author_fact(team=None) appends only while holding the same state lock (an exclusive flock across processes, re-entrant per thread, per store.rs). A CLI append therefore cannot fall between the admission snapshot and the scan.
Receive and publish paths (store_fact) also append under the lock, and broadcasts made inside the pickup defer until the lock is released.

The test idle_fact_pickup_skips_admission_and_concurrent_cli_appends_survive runs 12 concurrent standalone author_fact writers against pickups. It asserts that all 12 facts survive both on disk (load_facts) and in memory (disabled_connections).
residual_notes: The concurrency test is probabilistic and does not deterministically force the old window. The guarantee is structural: one lock-held transaction.

evidence: Under the lock, fact_file_stamp captures (inode, length, mtime, mtime_nsec) of facts.jsonl. When it equals the stored stamp, pickup returns before load_facts, so an idle poll does no fold and no signature verification.
The stamp is recorded only after a completed pickup, under the same lock. Any `?` error leaves it unchanged, so the next poll retries.

Appends change the length. Quarantine and load_facts rewrites go through write_bytes (tmp file and rename), which gives a new inode. Changes made during the pickup are therefore folded into the recorded stamp rather than missed.
The test asserts that 12 idle pickups do not increment fact_pickup_loads.
residual_notes: Cost is now driven by change rather than by polling. A received or appended fact still triggers one full cold load on the next pickup, and refold runs load_facts once per newly inserted fact within that pickup. This is acceptable but grows with fact count during bursts.

A change could theoretically go undetected if inode reuse, identical length and identical mtime to the nanosecond all coincide. On a filesystem with coarse timestamps this is improbable but not impossible.
